memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: As the Lord commanded his servant Moses, so Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua did it; he left nothing undone of all that the Lord commanded Moses - Josh 11:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a testimony to be written about a man's life: "he left nothing undone of all that the Lord commanded." The chain of faithfulness is complete here — the Lord commanded Moses, Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua did it. Each link held. God spoke, and generation by generation His word was carried out.

Joshua's obedience was not selective. He did not pick the parts that suited him and quietly drop the rest. He left nothing undone. Most of us obey God in pieces — the convenient commands, the ones that cost little. But Joshua stands as a picture of wholehearted obedience, the kind that follows through to the end.

And yet even Joshua was not perfect; later chapters show Israel's obedience was incomplete in the long run. Joshua points us to a better and greater Joshua — Jesus, whose very name is the same. Of Him alone can it be said with no exception that He left nothing undone of all the Father commanded. On the cross He cried, "It is finished" (John 19:30). Every command kept, every requirement met, every debt paid. Our salvation does not rest on our patchy obedience but on His perfect and complete work. That is why we can obey freely now — not to be saved, but because we are.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- If your life were summed up in one line, what would it say about your obedience?
- Where do you tend to obey in pieces rather than wholeheartedly?
- How does Christ's finished work free you from earning God's acceptance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You left nothing undone of all the Father gave You to do. Because Your work is finished, I rest in You and follow You gladly. Amen.
